correctness.rationale: A subset 1-fair dominates a disconnected clique union iff each component contains exactly one selected vertex or is entirely selected. For potential coalitions with total size<=4, only size-three full transversals work. An excess d=sum(|B|-1)<=2 forces singleton components requiring at least three separate complementary doubletons, contradiction; three cross-pair doubletons realize d=3. For equality d=3, the four-block and triple+double shapes cannot serve singleton vertices in multiple components; three doubletons have component pair counts (1,1,1),(2,1,0),(3,0,0), with the latter types possible only when their depleted components have size 3. Counting individually labelled choices produces T=prod_i n_i(n_i-1)+3 sum_{i:n_i=3} n_j n_k(n_j+n_k-2)+6 sum_{i<j:n_i=n_j=3}1. Independent disjoint-edge matching enumeration reproduced T(3,3,3)=558 and T(3,3,4)=798; universality comes from combinatorial proof.

value.rationale: Exact optimum and complete equality-family census for three disconnected cliques is a natural structural invariant in a recently introduced domination theory. Size-three exceptional branches and explicit labelled partition counts are substantive beyond a routine bound.

final_claim: For three disjoint labelled cliques of sizes n_i>=3, the 1-fair coalition number is N-3, every optimum partition uses three cross-clique doubletons, and the exact labelled-vertex unordered-partition count is product n_i(n_i-1) plus the stated size-three corrections.
limitations: Exactly three components each of size at least three; counts unordered partitions of labelled vertices, not coalition-partner witness choices.
